newsitem.title: USA: Pounding rain brings floods to western Washington.
newsitem.headline: Pounding rain brings floods to western Washington.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke declared a state of emergency in five rain-soaked Olympic Peninsula counties Wednesday after rising rivers forced hundreds of people from their homes.
Up to 21 inches of rain in western Washington over the past four days has sent 17 rivers over their banks, destroyed homes and livestock and closed 20 roads.
Locke's declaration activated the National Guard to help with sandbagging and rescue efforts and freed emergency funding in Clallam, Grays Harbor, Kitsap, Mason and Jefferson counties.
Grays Harbor County on the coast was particularly hard hit with 21 inches of rain over four days including nine inches in 24 hours near Montesano, about 75 miles (120 km) southwest of Seattle.
More than 300 homes were evacuated as the Wynoochee, Satsop and Chehalis rivers overflowed their banks and rose to near record levels.

Dave Storm, a hydrologist with the National Weather Service, said the heavy rains were caused by a massive stream of warm, wet air from the Pacific Ocean south of Hawaii, but he said cooler, drier weather was in the forecast.
"It has been diminishing and we should be pretty close to the end of the heavy rain," he said. "By 10 tonight things should be pretty well shut off."
Mud slides, which have caused serious problems since an unusually heavy snowstorm hit the state in late December, continued to take a toll, destroying several homes.

In Seattle's exclusive Magnolia section, where some residents have been unable to return to their homes since the December storm, another 18 homes were evacuated after a slide carried one house and its occupant into the road. The homeowner was not injured.
Another house across Puget Sound on Bainbridge Island, which already had been labeled as uninhabitable, also was destroyed by a mud slide.
Weather Service forecasters said that while most rivers were at or near peak levels, they were concerned about additional flooding possible in Mount Vernon, 60 miles (90 km) north of Seattle.
